To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ectopic endometria and the embryonic residues identified in the fetal female reproductive tracts have a similar immunophenotype and may play a role in the development of gynecological diseases in adulthood.

the ectopic organoids identified in female fetuses are composed of endometrial-like epithelial and stromal components, as well as embryonic duct residues, which are not detected in adult endometriotic lesions.
misplaced endometrial-like tissue in the fetal female reproductive organs may play a role in the development of adult gynecological diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of ectopic endometrium and embryonic ducts in the female reproductive organs of the fetus.
a better comprehension of the origin and the pathogenetic role of misplaced endometrium and embryonic duct remnants in pelvic gynecological pathologies.
the possible pathogenetic role played by displaced endometrial glands as well as embryonic ducts remnants in the development of endometriotic and neoplastic pelvic gynecological disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
endometriosis, ovarian and uterine cancer may develop on the base of displaced endometrial glands or remnants of the embryonic ducts.

the embryonic residues and the endometrial tissue misplaced in the myometrial and the ligamentous structures are the possible pathogenetic basis for the development of endometriosis, ovarian and pelvic tumors.
the embryonic ducts and misplaced endometrial tissues could be considered as the possible pathogenetic factors in endometriotic and pelvic neoplastic processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the embryonic residues may be a possible pathogenetic substrate for endometriosis, ovarian neoplasms, and pelvic neoplasms.
endometriosis may develop on the base of misplaced endometrium.

endometrial glands can be found outside the uterus in fetal female reproductive system, in the myometrial layer and in the uterocervical region, as well as in the fallopian tubes and in the uterosacral and ovarian ligaments, where the embryonic duct remnants are localized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endometrial tissue and embryonic ducts may be the precursors of the ectopic endometriotic and neoplastic lesions in adult women.
the ectopic endometriotic glands and embryonic residues may be the basis for the development of endometriotic lesions and neoplastic disease.
endometriosis, ovarian and endometrioid endometrial cancers may develop on the base of misplaced endometrium and/or embryonic ducts residues.
